long_biography.plain_text:
Born in Pittsburgh, Hillman studied geology at Princeton and became a US Navy aviator during the Second World War. He joined Pittsburgh Coke & Chemical after returning home, learned the family operations, and assumed leadership when his father died in 1959. Rather than preserve the inherited structure, he sold legacy industrial businesses and redirected capital towards new sectors.

Hillman combined patient backing with a willingness to enter emerging fields before they became conventional. His investments reached technology, healthcare, energy and urban development, while his family foundations concentrated giving in western Pennsylvania. With his wife Elsie, he supported cancer care and research at UPMC and advanced work in computing, transport and neuroscience at Carnegie Mellon. That blend of reinvention and local commitment made him both a national investment pioneer and a defining civic figure in Pittsburgh.
